node.label: Callum G. Brown
node.date_label: Religion and Society in Scotland since 1707: listed edition 2 (1997) · The Death of Christian Britain: first edition (2001) · Postmodernism for Historians (2005) · Religion and Society in Twentieth-Century Britain (2006)
node.description: A social and cultural historian of religion, secularisation and unbelief. Brown’s work moved from class-based measurements of church participation toward the gendered and discursive conditions of Christian identity, with a sharp rupture proposed for the 1960s. That account remains contested. Jeremy Morris accepts criticism of inevitable modernization-to-decline stories while arguing that Brown and others narrow religion too far: institutional decline can coexist with persistent religious identity. Brown’s later “The Necessity of Atheism” approaches the problem from another direction. Using Charles Taylor as a critical foil, he argues that measuring secularity only through religious categories marginalizes lives lived without a god and that medieval disbelief should not be ruled out in advance. The intervention challenges both the assumed religious past and the categories used to describe the secular present; it does not establish a single universal measure of unbelief.
